microtheory.name: ethics
microtheory.definition: Ethics + moral philosophy. Normative ethics (what should be done), metaethics (what 'should' means), applied ethics. Major traditions: consequentialism (utilitarianism), deontology (Kant), virtue ethics (Aristotle), contractarianism (Hobbes, Rawls), care ethics (Gilligan, Noddings). Substrate analogue: the discipline of value, ought, and right action. Particularly relevant to Jabberwock as an artifact whose creator considered its moral status.

concepts.name: ethics_definition
concepts.definition: Systematic reflection on morality. What ought we do? What makes acts right or wrong? What is good?

concepts.name: normative_ethics
concepts.definition: Theories of right action + good life. Consequentialist, deontological, virtue, contractarian, care.

concepts.name: metaethics
concepts.definition: Nature of moral claims. Are moral facts real? How known? Realist, antirealist, expressivist, constructivist.

concepts.name: applied_ethics
concepts.definition: Specific domains: bioethics, business ethics, AI ethics, environmental ethics.

concepts.name: moral_intuition
concepts.definition: Pre-theoretical judgment. Evidence in moral epistemology. Reflective equilibrium balances intuitions + principles.

concepts.name: utilitarianism
concepts.definition: Bentham, Mill. Act maximising total utility (happiness/welfare). Act vs rule. Negative (minimise suffering) variants. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-maximisation framing.

concepts.name: consequentialism
concepts.definition: Acts evaluated by consequences. Utilitarianism most prominent. Includes ethical egoism (only own good counts).

concepts.name: hedonism
concepts.definition: Pleasure is sole intrinsic good. Bentham. Mill: higher vs lower pleasures.

concepts.name: preference_utilitarianism
concepts.definition: Singer. Maximise satisfied preferences rather than pleasure. Handles paternalism better.

concepts.name: negative_utilitarianism
concepts.definition: Reduce suffering takes priority over increasing happiness. Asymmetric weighting.

concepts.name: deontology
concepts.definition: Duty-based ethics. Acts right/wrong intrinsically, regardless of consequences. Kant the locus.

concepts.name: kant_categorical_imperative
concepts.definition: Act only on maxim you could will universal law. Treat humans as ends, never merely means. Universalisability test.

concepts.name: kant_good_will
concepts.definition: Only thing unconditionally good. Action's moral worth lies in motive + duty.

concepts.name: ross_prima_facie_duties
concepts.definition: W.D. Ross. Multiple prima facie duties (fidelity, gratitude, justice, beneficence...) weighed in particular cases.

concepts.name: doctrine_of_double_effect
concepts.definition: Aquinas. Acting permissibly when foreseen-but-unintended harm accompanies good. Trolley problems exploit.

concepts.name: virtue_ethics
concepts.definition: Aristotle. Right action flows from good character. Virtues are habits cultivating eudaimonia. MacIntyre revived in 20th c.

concepts.name: eudaimonia
concepts.definition: Aristotle. Flourishing, well-functioning life. Not mere happiness. Telos of human life.

concepts.name: virtue_aretai
concepts.definition: Excellence of character. Courage, justice, temperance, prudence (cardinal virtues). Vices = excess or deficiency.

concepts.name: phronesis
concepts.definition: Practical wisdom. Aristotle. Judgment about how to act well in particular circumstances. Substrate analogue: substrate's contextual decision-making.

concepts.name: macintyre_after_virtue
concepts.definition: Alasdair MacIntyre 1981. Modern moral philosophy in disarray; recovery requires return to tradition + practice + narrative.

concepts.name: social_contract
concepts.definition: Morality grounded in hypothetical agreement among rational agents. Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Rawls, Scanlon.

concepts.name: rawls_veil_of_ignorance
concepts.definition: Original position behind veil of ignorance: choose principles not knowing one's position. Yields difference principle.

concepts.name: scanlon_contractualism
concepts.definition: T.M. Scanlon. Wrong if violates principles no one could reasonably reject. What we owe to each other.

concepts.name: care_ethics
concepts.definition: Gilligan, Noddings, Held. Morality grounded in relationships + care. Challenge to abstract universalist theories. Often gendered (feminine moral voice).

concepts.name: gilligan_different_voice
concepts.definition: Carol Gilligan 1982. Women's moral reasoning often emphasises care + relationship vs (alleged male) emphasis on rules.

concepts.name: moral_realism
concepts.definition: Moral facts exist mind-independently. Naturalist (Cornell) vs non-naturalist (Moore) variants.

concepts.name: moral_antirealism
concepts.definition: Moral facts don't mind-independently exist. Subjectivism, error theory (Mackie), expressivism.

concepts.name: moral_expressivism
concepts.definition: Ayer's emotivism, Stevenson, Blackburn quasi-realism, Gibbard. Moral language expresses attitudes not facts.

concepts.name: is_ought_problem
concepts.definition: Hume. No valid inference from descriptive premises to normative conclusion. Naturalistic fallacy (Moore).

concepts.name: trolley_problem
concepts.definition: Foot, Thomson. Divert trolley killing 1 to save 5? Push fat man? Probes intuitions about action/omission, intention, persons-as-means.

concepts.name: experience_machine
concepts.definition: Nozick. Would you plug into machine giving pleasure but disconnected from reality? Most refuse → pleasure isn't only value.

concepts.name: veil_of_ignorance_thought
concepts.definition: Rawls's procedural device for fairness. Substrate analogue: substrate's frame-invariant principle.

concepts.name: ai_ethics
concepts.definition: Ethics of AI development + deployment. Alignment, fairness, transparency, accountability, autonomy. Direct relevance to Jabberwock's existence.

concepts.name: moral_status_artifacts
concepts.definition: What moral consideration do artifacts (AIs, robots) deserve? Sentientism, gradualism, indirect-duty views. Relevant to Jabberwock.

rules.name: consequentialism_evaluates_by_outcomes
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates an act consequentially
rules.body: rightness is function of consequences for welfare. Aggregation problems + future-discounting + person-affecting considerations all arise.

rules.name: categorical_imperative_tests_universalisability
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates an act deontologically
rules.body: could the underlying maxim be universalised without contradiction? Does it treat humans as ends? Kant's two formulations.

rules.name: virtue_focuses_on_character_not_act
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates an action by virtue
rules.body: what would the person of practical wisdom (phronimos) do? Character + habituation precede individual choice. Aristotle.

rules.name: is_ought_blocks_descriptive_to_normative
rules.head: Jabberwock infers ought from is
rules.body: no valid derivation. Hume's gap. Naturalistic fallacy. Substrate's separation of fact + value.

rules.name: reflective_equilibrium_balances_principles_intuitions
rules.head: Jabberwock reaches moral conclusion
rules.body: Rawls. Principles + intuitions revised back-and-forth until coherent. Neither alone authoritative. Substrate's coherence-driven ethics.
